## Search for part of words

Search for the letter R anywhere in the column (note the case sensitivity)

```{r}
library(NHSRdatasets)

data <- NHSRdatasets::ae_attendances

data |>
  dplyr::filter(stringr::str_detect(org_code, "R"))

```

## Filters with grouped data

As with `summarise()` and `mutate()` we can group within the function `filter()`

```{r}
data |>
  dplyr::filter(org_code %in% c("RQQ", "NAX")) |> 
  dplyr::arrange(period)
```

Adding the group with `.by()`

```{r}
data |>
  dplyr::filter(org_code %in% c("RQQ", "NAX")) |> 
  dplyr::arrange(period) |> 
  dplyr::filter(period == max(period), .by = org_code) 

```

## Filtering using `AND`

Find type 1 `AND` attendances over 10,000

```{r}
data |>
  dplyr::filter(type == '1', 
                attendances > 10000)

```

## Filtering using `OR`

Find type 1 `OR` attendances over 10,000

```{r}
data |>
  dplyr::filter(
    type == '1' |
      attendances > 10000
  )

```

## Over to you

- Filter by type 1 `attendances` 
- Count org_code (for a bonus point put this in order of submissions)
- Filter by at least 24 submissions per `org_code`

:::{.callout-tip collapse=false appearance='default' icon=true}
- Help can be found for any function by typing `?` before it on the console or putting the cursor into it and selecting F1
:::


```{r}
#| eval: true
#| echo: false
countdown::countdown(
  minutes = 10,
  color_border = "#005EB8",
  color_text = "#005EB8",
  color_running_text = "white",
  color_running_background = "#005EB8",
  color_finished_text = "#005EB8",
  color_finished_background = "white",
  margin = "0.9em",
  font_size = "2em"
)
```

## Answer - using count

```{r}
data |>
  dplyr::filter(type == '1') |>
  dplyr::count(org_code, sort = TRUE) |>
  dplyr::filter(n >= 24) # n is the default name for the column
```
